newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Congress suspends fugitive legislator.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Congress suspends fugitive legislator.

text.p: An ethics committee of the Philippine Congress on Thursday recommended suspension of a colleague who is being sought by police on charges of statutory rape of an 11-year old school-girl.
A police official said he believed the fugitive lawmaker, House of Representatives member Romeo Jalosjos, had fled to Indonesia.

Members of the ethics committee of the House of Representatives unanimously voted to recommend the suspension of Jalosjos for 60 days after a 72-hour deadline set by the legislature for him to surrender to the police expired.
The committee in a resolution warned its next step if he continued to evade the law would be to recommend his outright expulsion from Congress.

Jalosjos, a member of President Fidel Ramos's ruling coalition in the legislature, has evaded arrest since a Manila judge on December 26 issued 14 separate warrants of arrest against him for two counts of statutory rape and 12 acts of lasciviousness.

State prosecutors filed the charges after an 11-year-old girl gave a statement saying Jalosjos had sexual relations with her several times in his Manila apartment last year, paying her amounts ranging up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time.
The prosecutors said the girl's father brought her to the politician in exchange for money. The father faces a separate charge of exploitation.
Ramos last week personally ordered a manhunt for Jalosjos during mounting media criticism of the police failure to locate the lawmaker.

General Manuel Pepino, head of a police task force in the southern Mindanao region, said he has information that Jalosjos left the country on a speedboat from a southern beach resort on December 26 for Indonesia.
"I am 99.9 percent sure about this information my men gathered," Pepino told reporters in southern Zamboanga city.
Jalosjos' lawyer, Alfredo Lazaro, said the congressman had been in touch with him by telephone and that he was trying to convince him to give himself up.
"I expect in a few days' time, he'll be coming out," he said.
Jalosjos was earlier reported by some newspapers to have gone to Malaysia.
